A soft tube body lives inside a long irregular shell of accreted minerals fused into scavenged debris, hull scraps and its own vitrified bezoars: centuries of everything it ate, worn as architecture.\n\nIt is never hostile. It does not fight and barely notices you. But it crawls, slowly and without stopping, and whatever lies in its path is flattened or swallowed. Now and then a scaled tentacle lashes out and drags a nearby object — a crate, a door, a wall — into the shell.
